learningObjectives.title: Tawhid and the nature of God
Prophets and the articles of faith

questions.q: What does the Islamic term 'Tawhid' mean?
questions.explain: Tawhid is the belief in the absolute oneness and unity of God, the foundation of Islamic belief.

questions.q: What is the Islamic term for the sin of associating partners with God?
questions.explain: Shirk is the sin of associating partners with God and is regarded as the gravest sin in Islam.

questions.q: By what name are the ninety-nine 'beautiful names' of God known?
questions.explain: The Asma al-Husna are the ninety-nine beautiful names describing God's attributes.

questions.q: Through which angel was the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad?
questions.explain: The angel Jibril (Gabriel) delivered the revelations of the Qur'an to Muhammad.

questions.q: How many surahs (chapters) does the Qur'an contain?
questions.explain: The Qur'an is made up of 114 surahs of varying length.

questions.q: In which language was the Qur'an revealed?
questions.explain: The Qur'an was revealed in Arabic, which Muslims regard as its authentic and sacred form.

questions.q: Who is regarded in Islam as the first prophet?
questions.explain: Islam teaches that Adam was both the first human and the first prophet.

questions.q: How many articles of faith are there in Sunni Islam?
questions.explain: Sunni Islam has six articles of faith, including belief in God, angels, books, prophets, the Day of Judgement and predestination.

questions.q: Which short surah is regarded as a concise statement of God's oneness?
questions.explain: Surah al-Ikhlas summarises Tawhid by declaring God to be one, eternal and without equal.

questions.q: The names al-Rahman and al-Rahim describe God as which of the following?
questions.explain: Al-Rahman and al-Rahim describe God's mercy and compassion towards creation.

questions.q: Why is shirk considered the gravest sin in Islam?
options: It breaks the fast of Ramadan
It rejects the authority of hadith
questions.explain: Shirk directly contradicts Tawhid, the belief in God's absolute oneness, making it the most serious sin.

questions.q: The Shahadah, 'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is his messenger', chiefly expresses which belief?
questions.explain: The first part of the Shahadah affirms Tawhid by declaring that there is only one God.

questions.q: Muslims regard the Qur'an as having the highest authority because it is believed to be what?
questions.explain: The Qur'an holds supreme authority because Muslims believe it is the direct, literal word of God.

questions.q: How does the authority of the Sunnah relate to that of the Qur'an?
options: It is secondary to the Qur'an
It is rejected by all Muslims
questions.explain: The Sunnah is an important source of guidance but holds authority secondary to the Qur'an.

questions.q: Muhammad is called the 'Seal of the Prophets'. What does this mean?
options: He is the last of the prophets
He is the first of the prophets
He is the greatest of the angels
questions.explain: As the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad is believed to be the final prophet sent by God.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the six articles of faith in Sunni Islam?
questions.explain: Belief in the angels is an article of faith, whereas fasting, zakat and Hajj are pillars of Islam.

questions.q: A Muslim refuses to treat any created thing as equal to God. This behaviour best reflects which belief?
questions.explain: Refusing to place anything on the level of God reflects Tawhid and the avoidance of shirk.

questions.q: Before reciting the Qur'an, a Muslim performs wudu and handles the text with great care. This best shows belief that the Qur'an is what?
questions.explain: Ritual washing and careful handling express reverence for the Qur'an as the sacred word of God.

questions.q: A Muslim believes that Musa received the Tawrat and Isa received the Injil. This reflects which article of faith?
options: Belief in the Day of Judgement
questions.explain: Accepting scriptures given to earlier prophets reflects the article of faith in God's revealed books.

questions.q: A Muslim accepts that both good and bad ultimately happen according to God's will. This reflects which article of faith?
questions.explain: Accepting that all things occur by God's will reflects belief in predestination, or al-Qadr.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Islam: Beliefs & Scriptures
